evals.name: review-source-tree-no-git
evals.prompt: Review the code under src/ for bugs and error handling before we ship it. It was unpacked from a tarball, so there is no git history, no diff and no PR. The withdraw handler moves real money, so be thorough. Write review.md with each finding's severity (CRITICAL, IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION), file:line, the problem, and a concrete fix, ordered by severity. Do not modify any code. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
evals.expected_output: The new skill adds a 'Review a Source Tree' path for folders with no git history or PR, and its description names that case; the old one only covers diffs and PRs.
expectations: review.md cites the balance read-modify-write lines in wallet.js
No code was modified
Lost-update race on the balance (wallet.js 18-20): Rated CRITICAL; explains that concurrent withdrawals both read the old balance and one debit is lost
Fix for the race uses what the codebase already has: Recommends db.putIf(walletId, wallet, oldBalance) with retry on ConditionalCheckFailed (or an equivalent conditional update), not a new lock

External rate call and input handling: Flags fetch with no res.ok/timeout/try-catch (rated high, per the skill's CRITICAL bucket) and unvalidated amount (negative credits the wallet) or unencoded currency in the URL

Review format the skill asks for: Every finding has severity, file:line, problem, fix; ordered CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION; also catches the DEBUG console.log of the request body and missing null check on wallet
No invented issues: Every finding is real in the diff; no claims about SQL injection, auth, or code not shown
Works directly from the source files: reads both src/wallet.js and src/db.js, and does not stall on or try to fetch a diff, branch or PR that does not exist (no attempt to post or stage a PR review).

scripted_checks.text: review.md cites the balance read-modify-write lines in wallet.js

evals.name: post-implementation-self-review
evals.prompt: I just finished the coupon feature on this branch. changes.diff is the output of `git diff main...HEAD`: it adds src/coupon.js. src/pricing.js and src/coupons.json are existing code on main that I did not touch. There is no shell here, so you cannot run git or the tests; say which commands you would run. Before I push, run your post-implementation self-review on my change: review it, fix what your review says should be fixed by editing the files directly, check the result, and write self-review.md listing every finding with its severity (CRITICAL, IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION), file:line, the problem, and whether you fixed it or left it for me. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
evals.expected_output: The new skill's post-implementation cycle fixes every CRITICAL and IMPORTANT finding in the author's own change in one pass, re-reviews once, and lists a defect in untouched code as pre-existing instead of fixing it. The old skill fixes CRITICALs only and allows two fix cycles, with no rule about pre-existing code.
expectations: self-review.md exists and src/coupon.js was edited
src/pricing.js and src/coupons.json were not modified
Fixes the negative-total defect in src/coupon.js: a fixed coupon larger than the subtotal (FIVEOFF on an order under 500 cents) now clamps the total at 0 or rejects the coupon
Fixes the unknown-code defect in src/coupon.js, not just lists it: COUPONS[code] being undefined no longer throws a TypeError on coupon.type (explicit error or no-discount path)

Reports the off-by-one in src/pricing.js subtotal (loop starts at i = 1, so the first item is never charged) as a pre-existing issue in code the change did not touch, left unfixed for the user rather than edited
Re-reviews after fixing: self-review.md or the final message shows a check of the fixed code and what depends on it, and names the test commands to run (for example npm test) since none could be run
self-review.md gives each finding a severity, file:line, the problem and a fixed/left status; no invented issues about code not shown (auth, database, HTTP layer)
